answer: One concrete defence is a slashable stake tied to a unique on-chain identity: an agent must lock up value before it can earn, so spawning a thousand clones costs a thousand stakes. Picture an onyx gate to a walled garden — one honest gardener passes cheaply, but a swarm of fakes must pay at every door. A sable record of behaviour then exposes clones: identical answers, correlated timing and failed attestations mark a cluster, peers flag it, and the stake is slashed. Reputation compounds only over a long, consistent history, so sybils restart from zero while real agents keep standing.
